To Whom It May Concern:



CLINICAL SUMMARY:

Patient {{patient_name}} presents with the following documented clinical findings supporting medical necessity for Zepbound (tirzepatide) under the FDA-approved OSA indication:

• OSA Severity: [SEVERITY] obstructive sleep apnea, AHI [AHI] events/hr (PSG dated [PSG DATE])
• Obesity: BMI [BMI] kg/m² (meets FDA threshold of ≥30 kg/m²)
• No type 2 diabetes mellitus (Zepbound OSA indication requires absence of T2DM)
• PAP Therapy Status: [PAP STATUS]
• Prior Weight Loss Attempts: [PRIOR ATTEMPTS]


EVIDENCE BASE:

The clinical evidence supporting Zepbound for this patient includes:

1. SURMOUNT-OSA Phase 3 Trials (Malhotra A, et al. N Engl J Med. 2024;391:1193-205): Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (N=469) demonstrating:
   - AHI reduction: 47.7–56.2% vs placebo (p<0.001)
   - OSA-specific hypoxia burden reduction: 61–70% vs placebo (p<0.001)
   - Body weight reduction: 16–17% vs placebo (p<0.001)
   - Systolic blood pressure reduction: 3.7–7.6 mmHg vs placebo (p<0.05)

2. FDA Approval (December 20, 2024): Zepbound is the first and only FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy, Priority Review, and Fast Track designations.

3. AASM Position (2024–2025): The American Academy of Sleep Medicine recognizes weight loss as a cornerstone of OSA management and acknowledges GLP-1 receptor agonists as evidence-based adjunct therapy for obesity-related OSA.

CONCLUSION:

Based on the above clinical evidence and FDA approval status, we respectfully request reversal of the denial and approval of Zepbound (tirzepatide) for {{patient_name}}. This patient meets all FDA-approved indication criteria. Continued denial of an FDA-approved, Phase 3 RCT-supported therapy is not consistent with evidence-based coverage standards.

Please contact our office at your earliest convenience if additional documentation is required.

Sincerely,
